title: Checklist: Roads, Internet and Shopping
summary: Traffic rules, cyber safety and consumer rights - every point in simple words.
keyPoints: In a money fraud, call 1930 at once and report on cybercrime.gov.in - the first hour matters most.
Never share your OTP, PIN or password; a UPI PIN sends money and never receives money.
After an accident, stop, help the injured, call 108 or 112, and inform the police.
For a traffic fine, check and pay only on the official e-Challan site, never through a link in an SMS.
For a consumer problem the seller does not fix, call 1915 or file on the e-Daakhil portal.

body.text: Part two of your checklist: the road, the internet and shopping. These are the rules you use almost every day.

items: 37. Driving licence. Carry the right licence for the vehicle you drive.
38. Vehicle papers. RC, insurance and PUC (pollution) certificate. DigiLocker copies are accepted.
39. Helmet and seat belt. Wear a helmet on a two-wheeler and a seat belt in a car.
40. Signals. Obey traffic lights, road signs, lane markings and police hand signals.
41. Speed limit. Stay within the limit for that road and vehicle.
42. Drunk driving. Driving after drinking is illegal and dangerous, and can lead to arrest.
43. Mobile phone. Do not use your phone while driving.
44. Wrong side. Never drive on the wrong side. Follow lane and overtaking rules.
45. After an accident. Stop, help the injured, call 108 or 112, and inform the police.
46. Hit and run. Running away after an accident is a serious crime.
47. Challans. Check the fine on the official e-Challan site. Never pay through a link in an SMS.
48. Vehicle changes. Unauthorised modifications, wrong number plates and fancy lights are not allowed.
49. Pedestrians. Use crossings; drivers must give way.
50. Public transport. Know your safety rights and how to complain.
51. Online money fraud. Call 1930 and report on cybercrime.gov.in at once. Also tell your bank.
52. Identity theft. If someone misuses your Aadhaar, PAN, SIM or bank details, report it immediately.
53. OTP and UPI. Never share your OTP, PIN or password. A UPI PIN sends money - it never receives money.
54. Phishing. Be careful of fake bank links, courier messages, job offers and fake customer-care numbers.
55. Cyberstalking and threats. Online stalking and intimidation are offences.
56. Private images. Sharing someone's private photos without consent is a crime.
57. Online defamation. False and harmful posts can have legal consequences. Honest complaints are allowed.
58. Social media. Threats, hate content and impersonation are not allowed.
59. Copyright. Do not copy or sell others' images, music, films or software without permission.
60. Your personal data. You have rights over how your personal information is collected and used.
61. Account hacking. Report unauthorised access. Do not hack back.
62. Loan apps. Check that the lender is RBI-registered before taking an online loan.
63. Deepfakes and fake identities. Manipulated videos and fake profiles can be reported.
64. Work confidentiality. Do not leak your employer's data, customer information or passwords.
65. Right to safety. You are protected from dangerous goods and services.
66. Right to information. You can know the price, quality, quantity and ingredients.
67. Right to choose. No one can force you to buy something.
68. Right to be heard. You can raise a complaint and expect a reply.
69. Right to redressal. You can get a refund, replacement or repair.
70. Right to consumer education. You can learn your rights and how to complain.
71. Warranty. Read what the warranty covers and what it excludes.
72. Online shopping. Know the rules for cancellation, refund, returns and late delivery.
73. Misleading ads. False claims in advertisements are not allowed.
74. Bills and receipts. Keep proof of purchase, payment and messages.
75. Hidden charges. Check extra fees, service charges and cancellation charges before you pay.
76. Complaints. Call 1915 or file on the e-Daakhil portal if the seller does not fix it.

body.text: For any traffic fine, you can check and pay on echallan.parivahan.gov.in. A link in an SMS is never the safe way to pay.
In a financial fraud, the first hour matters most. Call 1930 immediately - it gives the best chance of freezing your money.
Never approve a UPI 'collect request' to receive money, and never scan a QR code to receive money. Both send money out.

practicalSteps: Save 1930, 1915 and the e-Challan website on your phone.
Keep digital copies of RC, licence, insurance and PUC in DigiLocker.
Save screenshots and transaction IDs before deleting any chat.
Read the return and refund policy before buying online.
exceptions: Some documents can be shown later at the police station or online within a set time in certain states.
Products bought for resale or business use are usually not covered by consumer law.

faqs.q: Is a photo of my documents enough at a traffic check?
faqs.a: Yes. DigiLocker or mParivahan digital copies are legally accepted.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer for a consumer complaint?
faqs.a: No. Consumer commissions are meant to be simple, and you can argue your own case.

misconceptions.myth: A UPI PIN is needed to receive money.
misconceptions.fact: No. A PIN sends money out. To receive money, you only share your UPI ID or number - never a PIN.
